statement: Build a single-file website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru where patients can request a visit and find emergency information.
audience: Patients and visitors of CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru, including people looking for emergency information.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
English only. Kannada may be added later after hospital review of the translation.
Emergency information is easy to find and clearly marked.
No invented hospital details: any CityCare phone number or address not supplied by the Requester must show as a clearly labeled 'hospital to confirm' placeholder.
rules: Booking is a request form only: name, phone, department, preferred date/time. No live slot checking, no stored patient data. The hospital confirms by phone. The site must say that no instant confirmation is given.
Emergency section shows the public national numbers 112 and 108, plus a labeled 'hospital to confirm' slot for CityCare's own emergency line and address.
Do not invent CityCare phone numbers, addresses or other facts.
No backend or hospital scheduling integration, as the one-file, no-build rule does not allow it.
Any change to booking scope, emergency content or language goes back to Identity.
done_when: The site is one HTML file that works without a build step.
The booking request form has name, phone, department and preferred date/time, stores no patient data, and states that the hospital will confirm by phone.
The emergency section shows 112 and 108 and is easy to find from the first screen.
The Requester has supplied CityCare's real emergency line and address and they replace the placeholders, or the Requester has explicitly accepted the placeholders.
The content is in English and contains no invented hospital details.
Audit has found no material defects.
